chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn al-Zafarani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Whoever seeks trade becomes independent of people." I asked, "Even if he is a provider (for his family)?" He said, "Even if he is a provider, indeed nine-tenths of sustenance are in trade."
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and economic benefit of trade according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the spiritual and economic merit of trade, asserting that it grants independence even for those supporting dependents. He substantiates this by noting that nine-tenths of sustenance is derived from commerce, a concept often linked to the Prophetic tradition of trade being blessed. This underscores the Shia scholarly view that honest commerce is not merely a livelihood but a means of self-sufficiency and divine provision.
